title: Israeli strike kills two guards at MSF clinic in Gaza; Israel says they were Hamas members
dek: Doctors Without Borders called it a direct attack on a marked clinic. Hours earlier, the son of Hamas's leader survived a strike that the group called an assassination attempt.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
An Israeli strike on a clinic run by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Gaza killed two of its guards on Friday night, the medical charity said, calling it "a direct attack on MSF". The Israeli military said the two men were Hamas members who also worked as security guards at the clinic. Neither account could be independently verified.

MSF said it was "devastated and outraged", that the clinic was clearly marked with its logo, and that it had shared the site's coordinates with the Israeli military. The deaths bring to 17 the number of its colleagues killed in Gaza, the group said. "We stand in solidarity with the families and loved ones of our colleagues. We call for accountability," MSF said.

The Israeli military said it had not targeted a hospital and that no medical infrastructure was damaged. It called the incident "another example of the Hamas terrorist organization embedding itself within international organizations", according to reports. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called attacks on health facilities and workers in Gaza "outrageous and unacceptable".

## Strike on Hamas leader's family

Earlier on Friday, at dawn, an Israeli air strike hit a home where Izzeldeen al-Hayya, the 29-year-old son of Hamas leader and chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya, was staying with his family. Hamas official Basem Naim said he survived, and Hamas sources said several relatives were wounded, including the Hamas leader's daughter-in-law, but no one was killed, according to reports. Reports differ on whether the strike hit Gaza City's Rimal district or Deir al-Balah.

Hamas called it an attempt to assassinate him, linked it to threats made against Khalil al-Hayya by Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz, and accused Israel of trying to undermine the October 2025 ceasefire. The Israeli military did not comment on that strike. Four of Khalil al-Hayya's other sons have been killed in Israeli attacks since 2008, the most recent in May this year.

The strikes follow the killing on Wednesday night of Khaled Abu Nada, a member of Hamas's political bureau and Gaza's deputy education minister, the third senior Hamas figure killed in three days. Khalil al-Hayya has said Hamas will consult other Palestinian factions on a response.

## The ceasefire's toll

Separately on Friday, one man was killed in a drone strike on a vehicle west of Jabalia and three bodies were recovered in Rafah, according to reports from Gaza. Gaza's health ministry says at least 1,705 Palestinians have been killed and 6,163 wounded since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025, and at least 74,772 since the war began in October 2023. The figures, which do not distinguish between civilians and fighters, cannot be independently verified. Israel says its strikes target militants who threaten its forces or violate the truce.

Gaza's civil defence agency warned that about 1.3 million people living in tents faced flooding from an approaching storm, according to reports.

## Why it matters for India

India welcomed the US-brokered ceasefire plan last year and has called for humanitarian access, the release of hostages and a negotiated two-state solution. Continued strikes on senior Hamas figures, including the movement's chief negotiator's family, put pressure on a truce whose later stages, including disarmament and Gaza's future governance, remain unresolved. A breakdown would add to instability in a region already shaken by the Gulf conflict, which affects India's oil supplies and the safety of its nationals working there.

## What happens next

MSF has called for accountability for its staff's deaths. Hamas has not announced its response after consulting other factions. The Israeli military says it will continue to act against threats in Gaza.
